To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 2-phase pattern of training, with a significant increase in the last 3 days, can provide a better taper than the optimal linear taper.
the final 3-4 days of the taper should be spent at a higher intensity than the preceding 2-3 weeks, and that the increase in intensity can be as large as 20-30%.
a final increase in the training load at the end of a taper can be beneficial for performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model that can predict the performance response to a given taper.
the development of mathematical models of training responses and performance.
the development of mathematical models of training responses, which are used in computer simulations to test different training strategies and to assess their potential performance benefits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a final increase in volume training during tapering is beneficial for performance in nonathletes and athletes, but the effect is very small.
the optimal tapering pattern is a combination of a reduction of training load and a final increase in the training load.
a 20% increase in training load in the final phase of a taper may be a useful strategy for athletes to achieve a higher performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a 2-phase pattern, characterized by a prolonged reduction in the first part of the taper and a subsequent increase in training load at the end of taper, is a more effective taper strategy than the traditional linear taper.
the final increase in training at a low intensity during the taper may allow a better adaptation and performance in athletes.
a final increase in volume during tapering may be a useful approach for athletes who want to achieve a maximal performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 2-phase pattern may be a useful tool for athletes who are not able to reduce their training load as much as the model predicts.
the last 3 days before a competition are crucial in the tapering process.
a final increase in exercise load at the end of a taper may be an alternative strategy to enhance the performance benefit of taper.
